propositions: The inbound link differ is add-only by construction and never removes local dependencies when a link is deleted in Jira, while the outbound direction has a removal path, creating an asymmetric sync behavior.
A link deleted in Jira persists on the local ticket indefinitely because no reconciliation pass evaluates the absence of links—only the presence of links in current Jira fields is processed.

The apply layer silently discards any non-add link record, so even if the differ were to emit a removal, the apply phase would drop it without error, violating the silent-failure detection this epic requires.

Determining whether a peer-side link deletion is real (versus failed enrichment) requires distinguishing observed-empty issuelinks from unobserved issuelinks, and tracking whether a link was ever pushed to the peer to avoid destroying never-pushed local-only deps.

The ecosystem research and first-hand production incident (63 parent edges destroyed) showed that inferring a peer deletion from managed-ref state alone cannot distinguish brand-new local links from truly deleted peer links, making the original arbitration design unsafe.

The shipped behavior is local-wins-and-restore: deleted peer links are re-added on the next pass, which is convergent and loses no local data, matching the behavior of mature integration tools that also decline to propagate peer-side relationship deletions.
